title: Former State Minister’s son arrested over Rs. 20M robbery - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The son of former State Minister Shanta Bandara has been arrested by the Colpetty Police in connection with the alleged robbery of Rs. 20 million belonging to a Chinese national.

Police said the 21-year-old suspect was taken into custody as part of an ongoing investigation into the incident, which allegedly took place on July 13.

Police said the robbery occurred while the Chinese national was transporting the cash in a vehicle.

Police have already arrested four other suspects in connection with the incident, all of whom have been remanded pending further investigations.

Police said that a grandson (19) of a prominent businessman is among those allegedly linked to the case.

The 21-year-old suspect is expected to be produced before court.

title: CIABOC begins probe on former Minister Akila Viraj - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Roshan Thushara

The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has launched an investigation into allegations that former United National Party (UNP) General Secretary Akila Viraj Kariyawasam committed an offence of corruption by recruiting employees to the Presidential Secretariat and deploying them for his personal and political activities.

As part of the ongoing investigation, Kariyawasam was summoned to appear before the Commission today (21) for further inquiries into the alleged use of Presidential Secretariat employees for political work.

However, CIABOC said that as of this afternoon, Kariyawasam had not appeared before the Commission and had not informed officials of any reason for his absence.

The investigation is being conducted under provisions of the Bribery Act relating to the misuse of public servants for private or political purposes, which constitutes an offence of corruption.

title: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra detained by Delhi Police amid protest near PM residence
summary: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained by the Delhi Police on Tuesday while leading a protest near Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s official residence at Lok Kalyan Marg, where Congress leaders were demanding accountability over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and seeking the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

title: Pakistan steps in as US-Iran war widens and Hormuz shipping stalls
summary: Diplomatic efforts intensified on Tuesday to revive the collapsed interim agreement between Iran and the United States, even as both sides continued attacks for a 10th day of renewed fighting. Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni travelled to Pakistan, which has been trying to mediate between the two countries, but it was not immediately clear what fresh arrangement could emerge to end the war.

title: Crossings dominate market activity as ASPI extends decline - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Almas Equities Research

The Colombo Stock Exchange ended Tuesday's session on a mixed note, with the ASPI closing lower despite a strong start to the day, as renewed selling pressure erased early gains. The benchmark index climbed nearly 70 points within the first 15 minutes of trading, supported by buying interest in selected large-cap counters. However, the momentum gradually faded as profit-taking and continued selling pressure weighed on the broader market, leaving the ASPI to finish the session in negative territory.

Although market turnover rose sharply compared to the previous session, the improvement was largely driven by high-value crossing transactions rather than broad-based investor participation. Retail sentiment remained cautious, while institutional and value-oriented investors continued to execute strategic block trades. The ASPI also edged closer to the key 21,000-point level, reflecting the prevailing cautious mood among market participants.

The ASPI declined by 62.31 points, or 0.29%, to close at 21,145.73, while the S&P SL20 Index edged up by 1.79 points, or 0.03%, to settle at 5,945.01. Total market turnover amounted to LKR 3.27 Bn, with 38.52 Mn shares traded.

The Food Retailing sector emerged as the largest contributor to market turnover, generating LKR 2.32 Bn with 4.32 Mn shares traded. CARG.N dominated sector activity, recording LKR 2.32 Bn in turnover on 3.69 Mn shares traded. Crossing transactions accounted for LKR 2.49 Bn, representing a substantial 76% of total market turnover, with the largest crossing recorded in CARG.N amounting to LKR 2.26 Bn involving 3.59 Mn shares.

Market breadth remained weak, with 133 decliners outweighing 76 gainers, highlighting continued selling pressure despite selective buying interest in several large-cap counters. DIAL.N was the largest positive contributor to the ASPI, adding 9.81 points, followed by JKH.N, LION.N, SEMB.X, and SPEN.N. On the downside, CINS.N exerted the biggest drag on the index, reducing it by 22.56 points, while COMB.N, RICH.N, CARS.N, and HARI.N also weighed on overall market performance.

Among notable trades, CARG.N generated LKR 2.32 Bn in turnover on 3.69 Mn shares traded, while the counter edged up by 0.04% during the session. Despite the significant increase in turnover, the dominance of crossing transactions and weak market breadth suggest that broader investor sentiment remains cautious as participants await stronger earnings-driven catalysts.

title: Govt. has purchased over 1,900 metric tons of paddy since July - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The government has purchased a total of 1,910 metric tons of paddy as of yesterday (20), Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

Speaking at the media briefing to announce Cabinet decisions today (21), the Minister said the Paddy Marketing Board (PMB) has spent Rs. 229.35 million on paddy purchases since the procurement programme commenced on July 13.

He said the government aims to purchase a total of 39,500 metric tons of paddy, with Rs. 6 billion allocated to the PMB for the programme.

In addition, a further Rs. 10 billion has been allocated under the ‘Odapana’ loan scheme to support the initiative.

Minister Jayatissa said the government had initially planned to open 143 paddy warehouses for the purchasing programme. However, as harvesting has not yet commenced in all areas, only 71 warehouses are currently in operation.

He noted that the 71 warehouses had purchased 1,910 metric tons of paddy by yesterday, with the PMB allocating Rs. 229.35 million for the procurement process.

title: My last days in Parliament: MP Archchuna - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Referring to his political future, independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna today said he is currently spending his last days in Parliament.

"I will not be in Parliament for long. I will be in Parliament for two more weeks only," he told the House.

He said the case filed by Oshala Herath asking the Judiciary to remove me from Parliament will create a wrong impression that Sinhalese people do not want independent MPs.

title: Dengue risk to remain high for next three weeks: Health Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The risk of dengue transmission in Sri Lanka is expected to remain elevated for the next three weeks, with the period leading up to mid-August identified as a high-risk phase, Cabinet Spokesperson and Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

Speaking at the Cabinet press briefing held today (21), he said dengue spread was currently under a certain level of control, with several districts showing signs of a decline in reported cases. However, he noted that three districts continued to remain a concern and required closer attention.

The Minister stressed that continuous cleaning of public and private premises was essential to prevent the spread of dengue, especially amid prevailing rainy conditions that create new mosquito breeding sites.

He said instructions had been issued to all state institutions to continue dengue prevention activities without interruption, adding that such measures would remain a priority during the next three weeks.

“Dengue cannot be controlled through cleaning campaigns conducted on a single day. Mosquito breeding sites continue to emerge, particularly due to the current weather conditions. Even within homes, mosquito larvae can breed in places that often go unnoticed. Therefore, prevention activities must be carried out continuously,” Dr. Jayatissa said.

He also called on Medical Officer of Health (MOH) and Public Health Inspector (PHI) officers to remain actively engaged in dengue control efforts, including carrying out fogging operations where necessary.

title: Full probe ordered into Homagama factory fire that killed five - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Labour Deputy Minister Mahinda Jayasinghe has instructed officials of the Labour Department to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the fire that broke out at a factory in the Katuwana Industrial Zone, Homagama, this morning (21), and submit a report urgently.

Five people were killed and several others injured in the tragic incident.

The Deputy Minister has instructed Labour Commissioner General Nadeeka Wataliyadda to pay special attention during the investigation to several key areas, including the immediate cause of the fire, whether proper fire safety and occupational safety standards had been maintained at the factory, and whether adequate safety facilities and emergency evacuation procedures were in place for workers.

The investigation will also examine whether the factory had complied with the provisions of the Factories Ordinance and other relevant occupational safety regulations, and whether any negligence or lapses had contributed to the incident.

title: Special Cabinet panel reviews preparedness for possible El Niño impacts - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The Special Cabinet Subcommittee and Officials' Committee appointed to assess measures in response to possible El Niño conditions met for the second time at the Presidential Secretariat yesterday (20).

The meeting, chaired by Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi, focused on preparedness measures to address the anticipated impacts of El Niño across key sectors.

Officials said that the World Meteorological Organization has forecast an 81% probability of El Niño conditions developing globally. In light of this, discussions centred on sectors likely to be most affected, including agriculture, food security, plantations, water management and energy.

The committee also reviewed short-, medium- and long-term action plans prepared by relevant government institutions to mitigate the potential effects of El Niño.

Attention was further drawn to forecasts issued by the Department of Meteorology, while members considered additional proposals to strengthen preparedness and minimise the impact on vulnerable sectors.

title: PM meets UK delegation on rabies eradication - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya today (21) held discussions with a delegation from the United Kingdom on implementing a more systematic and accelerated national programme to eradicate rabies, improve animal welfare and manage Sri Lanka's stray dog population.

The meeting, held at the Parliament Complex, brought together representatives from UK-based animal welfare organisation Battersea and the International Companion Animal Management Coalition (ICAM-UK).

During the discussion, the delegation proposed adopting the 'No Dog Left Behind' approach, which aims to vaccinate the maximum possible number of dogs over a three-year period instead of targeting the current 70% vaccination coverage. Experts said the strategy could significantly reduce the need for costly post-exposure rabies treatment.

The participants also discussed strengthening vaccination efforts through local government institutions to address the current shortage of veterinarians and overcome administrative challenges.

Attention was also drawn to the proposal to establish a Presidential Task Force to oversee the programme, initially in the Western Province before expanding it islandwide, treating rabies eradication as a national priority.

Experts further stressed the importance of using high-quality vaccines, maintaining a reliable cold chain for vaccine storage and distribution, and ensuring effective oversight by the central government.

Prime Minister Amarasuriya said the government considers both animal welfare and the elimination of rabies as key priorities and pledged the government's support to implement the national programme by addressing existing practical challenges in collaboration with local authorities, relevant ministries and international organisations.

The discussion was attended by Battersea representative Roxanne Sahar Nazir, ICAM representatives Dr. Elaine Francisca Hiby, Dr. Eric Joseph Brum and Mr. Patrick Gerard, as well as Colombo Municipal Council Chief Veterinary Officer Dr. M. Ijas.

title: LRH urges parents to bring key medical documents due to dengue surge - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The Lady Ridgeway Children's Hospital (LRH) in Colombo has issued an urgent notice requesting parents and guardians to bring essential medical documents when bringing children for treatment or clinic visits, as the hospital faces a sharp rise in pediatric admissions due to the ongoing dengue epidemic.

Hospital Director Dr. Pradeep Ratnasekera said the number of children seeking treatment has increased significantly, leading to heavy congestion at the country's premier children's hospital.

He said the cooperation of parents and guardians is vital to ensure children receive prompt and efficient medical care despite the increased patient load.

Accordingly, parents are requested to bring the following documents whenever they visit the hospital:

Dr. Ratnasekera said these documents will help medical staff provide faster and more effective treatment.

The hospital also requested the public's maximum cooperation during the current dengue outbreak. For further information, parents may contact the Director's Office of Lady Ridgeway Children's Hospital on 011 2693711 (Ext. 307).

title: Govt to revise power generation plan to boost renewable energy share - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The government will revise its electricity generation plans to increase the share of renewable energy beyond the current target while strengthening the national transmission network to maximise the use of renewable power, Minister of Energy Kumara Jayakody told Parliament today.

Responding to a question raised by an Opposition MP, the Minister said the existing power generation plan targets 70% of electricity generation from renewable sources, but the government intends to increase that share through revised planning.

He said the electricity transmission system would also be upgraded to enable greater integration of renewable energy into the national grid.

As part of these efforts, the Sampur–Kappalthurai electricity transmission line will be upgraded from a capacity of 300 MW to 600 MW, while four additional electricity transmission systems will be constructed to strengthen the network.

The Minister also said that President Anura Kumara Dissanayake had recently instructed the government to invest in the construction of the Northern 400kV electricity transmission system.

He said the project aims to facilitate the integration of the maximum possible amount of renewable energy into the national electricity system.

title: CAA raids 112 shops and restaurants near bus stands over consumer law violations - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) carried out 112 special emergency raids on shops and restaurants located near bus stands, transport hubs and major long-distance bus stops across the island on July 20 as part of a nationwide operation to protect consumers.

The CAA said the raids targeted businesses operating in areas frequently used by passengers and the public, with the aim of curbing unfair trade practices and ensuring compliance with consumer protection laws.

During the inspections, officials detected several violations, including the sale of beverages, snacks and packaged food items at prices exceeding the maximum retail price (MRP) specified by manufacturers.

Inspectors also found traders failing to display prices of bakery products and other food items in a manner clearly visible to consumers, while some packaged goods lacked essential information such as the date of manufacture, expiry date, batch number, and the name and address of the manufacturer.

In addition, expired food items were found displayed for sale at several outlets.

The CAA said legal action would be instituted against the shops and restaurants that violated the law, with cases to be filed in the relevant Magistrates' Courts under the provisions of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act.

The Authority warned that strict legal action would continue against traders selling goods above the prescribed prices or providing substandard food items to the travelling public. It added that similar special raids would be conducted continuously across the country.

Consumers were also urged to report unfair trade practices to the CAA's 1977 Complaints Unit during office hours.

title: French lawmakers expected to pass social media ban for children under 15 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
FRANCE 24 - French lawmakers are expected to approve a bill banning social media access for children under 15 on Tuesday, putting France at the forefront of similar efforts in the European Union.

Parliamentarians from the upper and lower houses reached a compromise on the bill's text on Monday, paving the way for a vote on its final adoption, which is expected to pass despite criticism from parties on the left.

"Tomorrow, France will become the first country in Europe to introduce a digital age limit to better protect our children online," French Digital Minister Anne Le Henanff said on X.

President Emmanuel Macron has championed the law as a flagship reform of his final term in office and pledged to enforce it by September, meaning another element of the bill, a mobile phone ban in secondary schools, would be in place by the beginning of the school year.

The social media rule is expected to be rolled out in two stages, the first blocking under-15s from creating new accounts from September 1. The ban would apply to existing accounts from January 2027, according to the text.

Lawmakers agreed on the need for regulation, as warnings have multiplied over the harmful affects of social media on children.

France's public health watchdog last year said platforms such as TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram were detrimental to adolescents, particularly girls, though it was not the sole reason for their declining mental health.

The agency said that one in two teenagers spends between two and five hours a day on a smartphone. In a report published in December, it said that some 90 percent of children aged between 12 and 17 use smartphones daily to access the internet, with 58 percent of them using their devices for social networks.

The report highlighted a range of harmful effects stemming from the use of social networks, including reduced self-esteem and increased exposure to content associated with risky behaviours such as self-harm, drug use and suicide. Several families in France have sued TikTok over teen suicides they say are linked to harmful content.

The two chambers had disagreed on their approach to a ban, however.

French Senators had opted for a two-tier system distinguishing between blacklisted platforms flagged as harmful to a child's development and those that could still be accessed with parental consent.

But the lower house's broader approach demanding social media platforms refuse new users under 15 and suspend accounts belonging to children under that age prevailed.

Exceptions are provided for sites such as online encyclopaedias and educational platforms.

The blacklisting system would have taken more time, including fresh consultations with the European Commission on the criteria, and carried a "small risk" of non-compliance with European law, said centrist Senator Catherine Morin-Desailly, in charge of the bill in the upper house.

The EU itself has been mulling a social media ban since a push by member states, including France, Greece and Spain, for limiting access.

Last week, EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said children should have "phased and gradual access" to social media.

Enforcement of regulations will also face the challenge of setting up effective age verification systems.

Lawmaker Laure Miller told AFP platforms will be expected to integrate "the tool or tools" of their choice for this purpose, with various options available or in the works, including an age-verification app unveiled in April by the European Commission.

After Macron's government suspended a flagship pensions reform last year, a social media ban could be his last major domestic change before he steps down in April 2027.

With the law's adoption, France would join a growing list of more than 20 countries that have taken steps toward regulating children's social media access.

In December last year, Australia became the first country in the world to require TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat and other top sites to remove accounts held by under-16s, or face heavy fines.
